title: Honest question after 6 months of AI-assisted trading: better process, same P&L. Is it me, or is that the ceiling?
author: Trend_tracker
selftext:
Honest accounting, 6 months of using AI daily in my trading:

What improved: my notes are organized, every thesis is written down, I catch my own emotional entries more often. Process-wise, night and day.

What didn't improve: P&L. Not measurably.

I think I know why. I mostly used AI as an advice machine — "what do you think of this setup?", "should I be worried about X?" It always had an answer: complete, plausible, agreeable. I felt smarter after every conversation and traded roughly the same.

So before I sink in another 6 months:

1. Has AI measurably improved your actual results? How would you even attribute that?  
2. If yes — walk me through the actual workflow: what goes in, what comes out, and which decision it changed. I don't care which model or app — the job, not the tool.  
3.If you tried and quit — what killed it?  
4.Is "asking it for opinions" the fundamental trap?

comments.author: Trend_tracker
comments.body: Not selling anything, and please don't sell me anything either — describe workflows, not products. "I use XYZ app" with no detail gets ignored; "I paste in my journal and it flags my repeated mistakes" is exactly what I'm after.

comments.author: Ok_Doughnut_189
comments.body: How about using it to further develop your strategy or to see what compliments your idea or if you can create an indicator to assist in your everyday trading, or a scanner / signal etc

replies.author: Trend_tracker
replies.body: Yes tried but didn't work well. Especially scanner/signal. Anything to share?

replies.author: Ok_Doughnut_189
replies.body: Have a conversation with the ai and figure out its limitations and what’s possible figure out what it can see and detect in price and movement, i feel like we limit the ai with our way of thinking and ai sometimes can’t do everything with that being said ask it directly and build a system that will compliment your strategy. Just the approach I’ve been taking lately but I’m far from being a professional in the field. Also the data you use matters alot.

replies.author: Trend_tracker
replies.body: Thx for sharing. Will try again. Yep also subscribed data servoce

comments.author: Rare_Inflation3178
comments.body:
I think the trap is asking AI for opinions.  
The biggest improvement for me came when I treated it like a research assistant instead of an advisor.  
It generates hypotheses, writes code, finds edge cases, and helps design validation tests. The final decision still comes from evidence, not from the model’s confidence.

replies.author: Trend_tracker
replies.body:
Great! Clearest answer I've gotten. "Research assistant, not advisor". But how to implement it?  
Can you walk me through the workflow? Appreciate it!

replies.author: Rare_Inflation3178
replies.body:
Here’s the workflow I use:

1. I start with a market observation or trading idea.
2. A research agent searches relevant papers and public sources for supporting evidence, contradictions, and possible failure conditions.
3. It turns the idea into a falsifiable hypothesis and defines what evidence would disprove it.
4. It helps design and implement the test, with the evaluation criteria fixed before seeing the result.
5. I decide whether to discard, refine, or paper-trade the idea based on the evidence.

So the trader supplies the original insight; the agent expands and challenges it rather than pretending to be the trader.

If you want, share one rough hypothesis and I can walk through what each stage would produce using that example.
